name: United States

demographics.notes: Third-most populous nation globally; sustained by stable net international migration offsetting domestic fertility decline, maintaining a more favorable demographic pyramid than East Asian or European competitors.

economy.notes: World's largest nominal economy and undisputed global financial anchor; the US dollar serves as the primary global reserve currency (~58% of allocated reserves) and vehicle for >85% of foreign exchange transactions; global leader in AI, cloud software, aerospace, venture capital, and biotechnology.
major_exports: Refined petroleum products, crude oil, and Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG)
Civil aircraft, aviation engines, and aerospace parts (Boeing)
Integrated circuits, semiconductor intellectual property, and design tooling
Pharmaceutical preparations and advanced medical biotechnology
Advanced defense systems and military equipment
major_imports: Consumer electronics, computers, and telecommunications hardware
Passenger motor vehicles and automotive parts
Pharmaceutical active ingredients and specialty chemicals
Industrial machinery, electrical equipment, and steel
Apparel, furniture, and consumer retail goods

military.defence_spending_pct_gdp_source: World Bank WDI (MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS), 2024 data, extracted from user-provided dataset (file last updated 2026-02-24)
military.arms_exports_source: World Bank WDI (MS.MIL.XPRT.KD), constant USD, from user-provided dataset
key_equipment_or_doctrines: Global Force Projection: 11 nuclear-powered aircraft carrier strike groups (Nimitz and Gerald R. Ford class) capable of deploying sovereign air wings anywhere in international waters
Fifth-Generation Stealth Air Dominance: F-35 Lightning II joint strike fighter, F-22 Raptor air superiority fighter, and B-2 Spirit / B-21 Raider stealth strategic bombers
Nuclear Triad Deterrence: Ground-based Minuteman III ICBMs, Ohio-class ballistic missile submarines with Trident II D5 SLBMs, and long-range strategic bombers
Undersea Supremacy: Virginia-class and Seawolf-class nuclear-powered fast-attack submarines (SSNs)
Unified Combatant Command Network: Global operational commands (INDOPACOM, EUCOM, CENTCOM, AFRICOM, SOUTHCOM, NORTHCOM) backed by 750+ overseas military facilities in 80 countries

primary_sources: Petroleum (36% of consumption - world's top crude producer at >13M bpd)
Natural gas (33% - world's top producer and leading LNG exporter)
Renewables (13% - wind, solar, and hydroelectric power)
Nuclear electric power (9% - largest commercial nuclear power fleet with 93 reactors)
Coal (9% - domestic thermal and metallurgical production)
energy.note: Net energy exporter following the shale revolution (hydraulic fracturing and horizontal drilling in Permian and Eagle Ford basins), providing strategic insulation against global oil supply shocks.

major_ports: Port of Los Angeles & Port of Long Beach (San Pedro Bay complex handling >30% of US containerized imports)
Port of Houston (Leading US port for foreign waterborne tonnage and crude/refined oil exports)
Port of New York and New Jersey (Premier East Coast container gateway)
Port of Savannah (Fastest-growing Southeastern logistics hub)
strategic_airports: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL - world's busiest passenger hub)
Memphis International Airport (MEM - world's premier express air cargo gateway for FedEx)
infrastructure.energy_grid_resilience: Continental electric system divided into three synchronous interconnections: Eastern Interconnection, Western Interconnection, and Texas Interconnection (ERCOT); faces aging transmission lines and rising demand from AI data center expansions.
infrastructure.digital_infrastructure: Foundational bedrock of the global internet, hosting the highest concentration of hyperscale data centers (Northern Virginia Data Center Alley) and primary transatlantic/transpacific submarine cable landing stations.

top_partners: Mexico (largest bilateral merchandise trading partner under the USMCA trade agreement)
Canada (second-largest trading partner, vital energy and critical mineral supplier)
China (major source of consumer and manufactured imports, subject to strategic tariffs and export controls)
European Union (core high-value trade, pharmaceutical, and investment partner)
Japan & South Korea (crucial high-tech, automotive, and semiconductor trade partners)
chokepoint_exposure: Panama Canal (essential maritime shortcut connecting US East Coast and Gulf ports to Asia)
Taiwan Strait (critical transit route for advanced semiconductor shipments and electronics)
Strait of Malacca & Bab el-Mandeb (indirect exposure via global supply chain disruption and allied trade)

core_competencies: World leader in frontier artificial intelligence architecture, large language models, and AI software frameworks
Dominance in advanced semiconductor chip design (Nvidia, AMD, Apple, Qualcomm) and EDA software (Synopsys, Cadence)
Global commercial and military aerospace leadership (Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman) and commercial space launch (SpaceX)
Biotechnology, mRNA genomics, pharmaceuticals, and synthetic biology
tech_vulnerabilities: Critical vulnerability on overseas outsourced semiconductor fabrication (over 90% of advanced logic chips <5nm fabricated in Taiwan by TSMC)
Severe dependency on Chinese refining of critical minerals (rare earth permanent magnets, processed lithium, cobalt, gallium, germanium)
Shortage of specialized domestic precision manufacturing workforce and skilled semiconductor fab technicians

land_borders: Canada (8893 km - world's longest undefended international border)
strategic_chokepoints_adjacent: Hawaiian Islands (central Pacific naval hub at Pearl Harbor)
Guam & Mariana Islands (vital forward-operating hub in the Second Island Chain)

politics.executive: President of the United States serves as Head of State, Head of Government, and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces; elected indirectly via the Electoral College for a 4-year term (limited to two terms by the 22nd Amendment).
politics.legislature: Bicameral United States Congress comprising the Senate (100 members, two per state, 6-year terms) and House of Representatives (435 members apportioned by population, 2-year terms).
politics.judiciary: Independent federal judiciary headed by the Supreme Court of the United States (9 justices appointed for life tenure with powers of constitutional judicial review).

nuclear.delivery_systems: Fully operational strategic nuclear triad: 400 silo-based LGM-30G Minuteman III ICBMs, 14 Ohio-class SSBNs carrying Trident II D5 SLBMs, and strategic bombers (B-2 Spirit stealth bombers and B-52H Stratofortresses carrying nuclear gravity bombs and AGM-86 ALCM cruise missiles).
nuclear.notes: Maintains 1,770 deployed strategic warheads with a total stockpile of ~5,044 nuclear weapons (SIPRI / US Department of State 2024). Undertaking a comprehensive multi-hundred-billion-dollar triad modernization (Sentinel ICBM, Columbia-class SSBN, B-21 Raider).

strategic_priorities: Deterring Chinese aggression against Taiwan and maintaining an open, rules-based maritime order across the Indo-Pacific
Reinvigorating core democratic treaty alliances (NATO Article 5, AUKUS, Quad, US-Japan-ROK trilateral)
Reshoring leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing to domestic soil (CHIPS and Science Act) and securing critical mineral supply chains
Preserving the global dominance of the US Dollar, international financial clearing primacy, and SWIFT enforcement leverage
Maintaining decisive technological superiority in artificial intelligence, quantum information science, and hypersonic defense
dependencies: Near-total reliance on Taiwan (TSMC) for commercial and defense-grade sub-5nm semiconductor chip manufacturing
Heavy reliance on Chinese refining for critical raw materials, battery precursors, and rare earth magnets
Supply chain dependency on Asian manufacturing for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and medical consumables
Reliance on allied host nations (Japan, South Korea, Germany, UK) for forward-stationed base access and logistics hubs
vulnerabilities: High national public debt exceeding $34 trillion with expanding annual fiscal deficits and interest servicing costs
Extreme domestic partisan polarization complicating long-term treaty ratifications and predictable foreign policy commitments
Simultaneous strategic overstretch: Facing simultaneous deterrence requirements in Europe (Russia), Indo-Pacific (China), and the Middle East (Iran/Houthis)
Fragile defense industrial production capacity: Peacetime munitions stockpiles (artillery shells, Patriot PAC-3 interceptors, long-range anti-ship missiles) take years to replenish
strengths: Exorbitant Privilege of the US Dollar: Unrivalled global financial hegemony enabling deficit financing and devastating economic sanction capabilities
Unmatched Global Power Projection: Sole military with the logistical capacity to deploy, sustain, and resupply massive multi-domain forces anywhere on Earth within 24-48 hours
Domestic Energy and Agricultural Abundance: Completely food and energy self-sufficient, insulating the homeland from foreign embargoes
Global Alliance Depth: Command of formal mutual defense treaties covering over 50 sovereign nations (NATO, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Philippines)
